The Hunter Nature NTR 4XL Travel Trailer Is Beefy, Compact, and Absolutely Packed
28 photos
Photo: Hunter Nature
What is more or less a common sight in the U.S. is… not so much on the European caravan scene. Beefy, utilitarian offroad travel trailers remain the exception, not the rule, here, but that's not what makes a unit like the NTR 4XL a standout.
This is one of the newest creations from Turkish company Hunter Nature, which previously made headlines for the Raptor offroad expandable trailer, which was actually a more evolved version of the original Campravan Raptor XC . Neither is still in production, with the company replacing them with the five-entry NTR series.
The NTR4X, which is now being sold as NTR 4XL in the UK by partner Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors and which you can see in the video tour at the bottom of the page, is the second largest entry in this series. NTR obviously stands for "nature" because this trailer takes you out into nature and lets you stay there for as long as you can manage resources.
While the aesthetics of the NTR 4XL are similar to the newer trailers from Camppass , which are also designed and produced in Turkey, Hunter Nature claims to have been one of the pioneers, if not actually the first manufacturer of truly offroad caravans in Europe. The company has been on the market since 1987, but only offered components and parts until 2019, when they started building their own units.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors They imagined those as European-compliant in every way, but with an edge over every other manufacturer in that they would be truly offroad units.
All this explains the beastly, utilitary, almost military-inspired aesthetic of the NTR 4XL. This is an offroad caravan, but at the same time, it's a unit that can offer accommodation to the entire family and cover the basic needs. It offers comfort throughout the year, and it does so with certain flair. It's not an elegant caravan in the strictest sense of the word, but that's not to say that it's not good looking.
The NTR 4XL is built on a steel chassis with a full aluminum body . It comes standard with KNOTT brakes, a single axle with independent spring suspension, and a pop-up roof with canvas sections. The pop-up roof system was designed specifically for Hunter Nature and it can be operated with a single hand thanks to pneumatic pistons and scissor mechanism.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors The pop-up roof adds 45 cm extra inside, so you get full standing height, but the trailer remains functional even with it closed. The manufacturer says that this allows for year-round use and even comfortable use in extreme temperatures: you pop the roof for extra ventilation in hot weather and hunker down with it closed in freezing temps.
Speaking of extreme weather, the NTR 4XL is fully insulated. However, a space heater is only offered as an optional extra, though it will be an actual necessity if you're planning adventures in the wintertime.
This floorplan comes in at 3.7 meters/12.1 feet of length in the body (5.1 meters/16.7 feet overall), 2.58 meters/8.4 feet of overall height with the roof closed, and 2.22 meters/7.2 feet in width. It's a compact towable even by European standards, which makes the high sleeping capacity it offers even more impressive.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors The British version (NTR 4XL) is described as a four-person caravan , but the original one (NTR4X) is actually rated for six people if you attach a double bed to the roof. The layout is the same for both versions, with a U-shaped dinette at the rear that converts into a double bed by dropping the table and two kids' bunks at the front.
In between these two, you get a compact galley kitchen on the campside, complete with a two-burner and sink combo, a sink, some prep space, and all-aluminum cabinetry. A nice fridge with freezer is available across the way, together with more (aluminum) cabinetry.
The bathroom is tucked between the bunks and the fridge, and it seems to be finished off in aluminum and fiberglass. It's a wet one, as you should have expected given the dimensions of the trailer, equipped with a slim vanity with a faucet, a separate shower, and an optional cassette toilet.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors Standard features include 410W of solar on the roof, a 200 or a 300Ah battery, AL-KO stabilizers, and electrostatic paint in military green or light gray. Not listed but shown in photos and the video below is an electric step and what looks like a large storage box on the front of the trailer.
The trailer can hold 140 liters (37 gallons) of freshwater and 75 liters (20 gallons) of gray. It doesn't have a black tank because you get the cassette toilet.
Options include the space heater, an outdoor shower complete with a shower curtain, an outdoor kitchen, and an e-mover that will help with parking.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors Empty weight of the NTR 4XL is at around 1,400-1,600 kg (3,086-3,527 lbs), while maximum permissible weight is 2,500 kg (5,511 lbs), so you can take plenty of stuff with you.
Neither Hunter Nature nor the British distributor offer prices , so you have to contact them for a quote if you like what you see.
Photo: Hunter Nature/Pilgrim Caravans Outdoors However, the description of the video below drops the £55,560 figure, which I take is for the complete unit shown, which also has the outdoor shower. That's approximately €66,500 or $73,800 at the current exchange rate, and above average pricing for a European caravan.
